haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: They still get the generic message, but no link is created and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q3: It works for 30 minutes after issue and only once. A successful reset or a newer link burns it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays usable; the password is checked before the token is burned, so used_at stays unset.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions, including the one that did the reset, are deleted. They are redirected to login and must log in again.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs and drops the job. The user is not told and must request again.
haiku-low.q7: The API creates the raw token and puts it in the link; the email job carries that finished link. Only its hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the raw token with SHA-256 and looks up the row where used_at is NULL and expires_at is later than database now().
haiku-low.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table: a count of the user's rows with issued_at in the last hour. Older requests fall out of the window; rows are kept at least one hour.
haiku-low.q10: Any unused link for that account gets used_at set to now() in the same transaction, before the new link is inserted.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: burn the token, update the password hash, delete all the user's sessions. The confirmation email is queued after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The conditional UPDATE matches only a live row; the second transaction gets 0 rows and shows the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same generic 200 message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: Over the limit (3 per rolling hour): rollback, no link created, no email sent. The user still gets the generic message.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes after issue and single use. It ends sooner if it is used (successful reset) or burned because a newer link was issued for the account.
sonnet.q4: Still live and usable. The form is shown again with the reason, and the token is not burned.
sonnet.q5: None; all sessions for the account are deleted, including the device that did the reset. The user is redirected (302) to the login page and must log in with the new password; no auto-login.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure and drops the job silently. The user is not told; they see the generic message and must request again. The failed send still counts toward the 3 per hour limit.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the raw token (32 random bytes), stores only its SHA-256, builds the link from BASE_URL + "/reset?token=" + raw, and puts the recipient and finished link in the enqueued job. The worker sends it as given.
sonnet.q8: It computes sha256 of the raw token from the link and selects the row where token_hash matches AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now(). A row means show the choose-password page; no row means the expired page.
sonnet.q9: In the password_reset_tokens table itself: the count of that user's rows with issued_at > now() - 1 hour (using the (user_id, issued_at) index). Old requests drop out as they age past one hour. Rows are kept at least 1 hour, and a later cleanup job can delete older ones.
sonnet.q10: Earlier live links are burned (used_at set to now() where user_id matches and used_at IS NULL) inside the same transaction, after the rate-limit check passes and before inserting the new token row, under the user row FOR UPDATE lock.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: the token is burned (used_at set), the user's password_hash is updated, and that user's sessions rows are deleted. The "password changed" email job is enqueued after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: The conditional UPDATE ... SET used_at=now() WHERE token_hash AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now() RETURNING user_id is the guard. Only one submit gets a row; the other gets 0 rows, rolls back and sees the expired page.
